what_this_is: DATA for do-work/judge-check-rows.mjs: how the person's check rows (record:check, kind check) are judged on a commit, a push or any other tool call, and every word it says. `unit_kinds` are the kinds a row's `kinds` may name; `json_file` picks the files whose whole new value is a unit's view; `fixture_key` is the key a path row's `*` takes when a fixture text is placed at its path; `fixture_kind` is the kind of a fixture unit of a row that names no kinds. `row_kind` and `fixtures_field` say what a check row being written looks like inside a tool call's input. {name} is filled from what was found.

words.refused_head: The person's check rows refuse this {kind}:
words.read_by_a_model: check row {rule} is read by a model only (it states no test), so it refuses nothing here: {says}
words.off: check row {rule} is marked Off, so it is not judged
words.fixtures_wrong_head: check row {rule}: its fixtures do not hold, so the row does not judge what it says:
words.no_fixtures: check row {rule} states a test and has no fixtures: give fixtures { pass: [...], refuse: [...] }, at least one of each, so the row proves it judges what it says
words.write_refused_head: This call writes a check row whose fixtures do not hold; fix the row (its test or its fixtures) first:
words.unreadable_json: {where} is not JSON, so its whole value was not judged: {why}
words.no_rows: give rows: the person's check rows ({ id, kind: "check", says, kinds?, a test, fixtures? })
